plan: Nehemiah 12:27-43, 44–13:3; Nehemiah 13:4-6a; Nehemiah 5:14-19; Nehemiah 13:6b-31; Malachi 1:1, 2-5, 6-14; Malachi 2:1-9

readings.title: The Gathering of the Levites
readings.subtitle: The priests and Levites are brought to Jerusalem for the dedication.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 12:27] And at the dedication of the wall of Yerushalayim they sought out the Lěvites in all their places, to bring them to Yerushalayim to perform the dedication with gladness, and with thanksgivings, and with singing, cymbals, harps and lyres. [28] And the sons of the singers gathered together from the countryside around Yerushalayim, from the villages of the Netophathites, [29] and from the house of Gilgal, and from the fields of Geḇa and Azmaveth – for the singers had built themselves villages all around Yerushalayim. [30] And the priests and Lěvites cleansed themselves, and they cleansed <dn>את</dn> the people, and <dn>את</dn> the gates, and <dn>את</dn> the wall.

readings.title: The First Procession
readings.subtitle: Two great thanksgiving choirs are appointed to march on the wall.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 12:31] And <dn>I</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> the rulers of Yehuḏah up on the wall, and appointed two large thanksgiving choirs, to go to the right on the wall toward the Dung Gate, [32] and after them went Hoshayah and half of the rulers of Yehuḏah, [33] then Azaryah, Ezra, and Meshullam, [34] Yehuḏah, and Binyamin, and Shemayah, and Yirmeyah, [35] and of the sons of the priests with trumpets: Zeḵaryah son of Yonathan, son of Shemayah, son of Mattanyah, son of Miḵayah, son of Zakkur, son of Asaph, [36] and his brothers Shemayah and Azar’ěl, Milalai, Gilalai, Ma‛ai, Nethan’ěl, and Yehuḏah, Ḥanani with instruments of songs of Daviḏ the man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, with Ezra the scribe before them. [37] And at the Fountain Gate and straight ahead of them, they went up the stairs of the City of Daviḏ, on the stairway of the wall, beyond the house of Daviḏ, as far as the Water Gate eastward.

readings.title: The Second Procession and Great Joy
readings.subtitle: The choirs meet at the House of God, and the people rejoice.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 12:38] And the other thanksgiving choir went over against them, and <dn>I</dn> behind them with half of the people on the wall, going past the Tover of the Ovens as far as the Broad Wall, [39] and above the Gate of Ephrayim, and above the Old Gate, and above the Fish Gate, and the Tover of Ḥanan’ěl, and the Tover of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate. And they stood still at the Gate of the Prison. [40] Then the two thanksgiving choirs took their stand in the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> and half of the deputy rulers with me, [41] and the priests, Elyaqim, Ma‛asěyah, Minyamin, Miḵayah, Elyo‛ěynai, Zeḵaryah, and Ḥananyah, with trumpets, [42] and Ma‛asěyah, and Shemayah, and El‛azar, and Uzzi, and Yehoḥanan, and Malkiyah, and Ěylam, and Ězer. And the singers sang aloud, with Yizraḥyah in charge. [43] And on that day they slaughtered great slaughterings and rejoiced, for <dn>Elohim</dn> had made them rejoice with great joy. And the women and the children also rejoiced, so that the joy of Yerushalayim was heard far away.

readings.title: Provisions for the Priests and Levites
readings.subtitle: Men are appointed over the storerooms for tithes and contributions.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 12:44] And on that day some were appointed over the rooms for the stores, for the contributions, for the first-fruits, and for tithes, to gather into them from the fields of the cities the portions required by the Torah for the priests and for the Lěvites. For Yehuḏah rejoiced over the priests and the Lěvites who stood up. [45] Both the singers and the gatekeepers guarded the charge of their <dn>Elohim</dn> and the charge of the cleansing, according to the command of Daviḏ and Shelomoh his son. [46] For in the days of Daviḏ and Asaph of old there were chiefs of the singers, and songs of praise and thanksgiving to <dn>Elohim</dn>. [47] And in the days of Zerubbaḇel and in the days of Neḥemyah all Yisra’ěl gave the portions for the singers and the gatekeepers, a portion for each day. And they set apart <dn>את</dn> what was for the Lěvites, and the Lěvites set apart <dn>את</dn> what was for the children of Aharon.

readings.title: Separation from Foreigners
readings.subtitle: The law is read, and the mixed multitude is separated from Israel.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 13:1] On that day was read from the Book of Mosheh in the hearing of the people, and in it was found written that an Ammonite and Mo’aḇite should not come into the assembly of <dn>Elohim</dn> forever, [2] because they had not met the children of Yisra’ěl with bread and water, and hired Bil‛am against them to curse them, although our <dn>Elohim</dn> turned the curse into a blessing. [3] And it came to be, when they had heard the Torah, that they separated all the mixed multitude from Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: Eliashib's Alliance with Tobiah
readings.subtitle: The high priest gives a temple storeroom to an enemy of Israel.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 13:4] And before this, Elyashiḇ the priest, having authority over the storerooms of the House of our <dn>Elohim</dn>, was a relative of Toḇiyah, [5] and he had prepared for him a large room, where previously they had stored <dn>את</dn> the grain offerings, <dn>את</dn> the frankincense, and <dn>את</dn> the utensils, and <dn>את</dn> the tithes of grain, the new wine and the oil, which were commanded to be given to the Lěvites, and the singers and the gatekeepers, and the contributions for the priests. [6] But in all this <dn>I</dn> was not in Yerushalayim, for in the thirty-second year of Artaḥshashta sovereign of Baḇel <dn>I</dn> came to the sovereign.

readings.title: The Governor's Integrity
readings.subtitle: Nehemiah recounts his refusal to take the governor's food allowance.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 5:14] Also, from the day <dn>I</dn> was commanded to be their governor in the land of Yehuḏah, from the twentieth year until the thirty-second year of Sovereign Artaḥshashta, twelve years, neither <dn>I</dn> nor my brothers ate <dn>את</dn> the governor’s food. [15] But the former governors who were before me laid burdens on the people, and took from them <dn>את</dn> bread and wine, besides forty sheqels of silver. Their servants also oppressed the people, but <dn>I</dn> did not do so, because of the fear of <dn>Elohim</dn>. [16] And <dn>I</dn> also worked strongly in the work on this wall. We did not buy any land. And all my servants were gathered there for the work. [17] And at my table were one hundred and fifty of the Yehuḏim and deputy rulers, besides those who came to us from the nations around us. [18] And that which was prepared for me daily was one ox and six choice sheep, and birds were prepared for me, and once every ten days plenty of all kinds of wine. And in spite of this <dn>I</dn> did not seek <dn>את</dn> the governor’s food, because the bondage was heavy on this people. [19] O my <dn>Elohim</dn>, remember me for the good – all that <dn>I</dn> have done for this people.

readings.title: Cleansing the Temple Storeroom
readings.subtitle: Nehemiah returns to Jerusalem and evicts Tobiah from the House of God.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 13:6] And after some days <dn>I</dn> asked leave from the sovereign to return, [7] and <dn>I</dn> came to Yerushalayim and learned of <dn>את</dn> the evil which Elyashiḇ had done for Toḇiyah, in preparing a room for him in the courts of the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>. [8] And it was very displeasing to me. Therefore <dn>I</dn> threw <dn>את</dn> all the household goods of Toḇiyah out of the room, [9] and <dn>I</dn> commanded them to cleanse the rooms. And <dn>I</dn> put back into them <dn>את</dn> the utensils of the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>, with <dn>את</dn> the grain offering and the frankincense.

readings.title: Restoring the Levitical Portions
readings.subtitle: Nehemiah confronts the rulers for forsaking the House of God.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 13:10] And <dn>I</dn> learned that <dn>את</dn> the portions for the Lěvites had not been given them, for each of the Lěvites and the singers who did the work had gone back to his field. [11] Then <dn>I</dn> contended with <dn>את</dn> the deputy rulers, and said, “Why is the House of <dn>Elohim</dn> forsaken?” And <dn>I</dn> gathered them together and set them in their place. [12] And all Yehuḏah brought <dn>את</dn> the tithe of the grain and the new wine and the oil to the storehouse. [13] And <dn>I</dn> appointed as treasurers over the storehouse Shelemyah the priest and Tsaḏoq the scribe, and Peḏayah of the Lěvites. And at their hand was Ḥanan son of Zakkur, son of Mattanyah. For they were reckoned trustworthy, and it was on them to distribute to their brothers. [14] Remember me, O my <dn>Elohim</dn>, concerning this, and do not wipe out <dn>את</dn> my loving-commitments that <dn>I</dn> have done for the House of my <dn>Elohim</dn>, and for its charges!

readings.title: Enforcing the Sabbath
readings.subtitle: Nehemiah stops commerce on the Sabbath day.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 13:15] In those days <dn>I</dn> saw in Yehuḏah those treading wine presses on the Sabbath, and bringing in sheaves, and loading donkeys with wine, grapes, and figs, and all kinds of burdens, which they brought into Yerushalayim on the Sabbath day. So <dn>I</dn> warned them on the day they sold food. [16] And men of Tsor dwelt there, bringing in fish and all kinds of goods, and sold them on the Sabbath to the children of Yehuḏah, and in Yerushalayim. [17] Then <dn>I</dn> contended with <dn>את</dn> the nobles of Yehuḏah, and said to them, “What evil matter is this that you are doing, profaning the Sabbath day? [18] “Did not your fathers do the same so that our <dn>Elohim</dn> brought all this evil on us and on this city? Yet you bring added wrath on Yisra’ěl by profaning <dn>את</dn> the Sabbath.” [19] And it came to be, when the gates of Yerushalayim were shaded before the Sabbath, that <dn>I</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> the doors to be shut, and commanded that they should not be opened till after the Sabbath. And <dn>I</dn> stationed some of my servants at the gates, so that no burdens would be brought in on the Sabbath day. [20] And the merchants and sellers of all kinds of wares spent the night outside Yerushalayim once or twice, [21] and <dn>I</dn> warned them, and said to them, “Why do you spend the night around the wall? If you do so again, <dn>I</dn> lay hands on you!” From that time on they came no more on the Sabbath. [22] And <dn>I</dn> commanded the Lěvites that they should cleanse themselves, and they should come, guarding the gates, to set apart <dn>את</dn> the Sabbath day. Remember me, O my <dn>Elohim</dn>, concerning this also, and pardon me according to the greatness of <dn>Your</dn> loving-commitment!

readings.title: Confronting Intermarriage
readings.subtitle: Nehemiah deals with the men who had married foreign women.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 13:23] In those days <dn>I</dn> also saw Yehuḏim who had married women of Ashdoḏ, Ammon, Mo’aḇ. [24] And half of their children spoke the language of Ashdoḏ, and could not speak the language of Yehuḏah, but spoke according to the language of one or the other people. [25] Then <dn>I</dn> contended with <dn>את</dn> them and cursed them, and struck <dn>את</dn> some of them and pulled out their hair, and made them swear by <dn>Elohim</dn>, saying, “You do not give your daughters as wives to their sons, nor take their daughters for your sons or yourselves. [26] “Did not Shelomoh sovereign of Yisra’ěl sin because of them? Among the many nations there was no sovereign like him, who was beloved of his <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>Elohim</dn> made him sovereign over all Yisra’ěl. Even him foreign women caused to sin. [27] “Should we then hear of your doing all this great evil, trespassing against our <dn>Elohim</dn> by marrying foreign wives?” [28] And one of the sons of Yoyaḏa, son of Elyashiḇ the high priest, was a son-in-law of Sanballat the Ḥoronite. And <dn>I</dn> drove him from me. [29] Remember them, O my <dn>Elohim</dn>, because they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood, and of the Lěvites.

readings.title: Final Reforms and Prayer
readings.subtitle: Nehemiah cleanses the people and appoints duties for the priests and Levites.
readings.text: [Nehemiah 13:30] Thus <dn>I</dn> cleansed them from <dn>את</dn> all that is foreign. And <dn>I</dn> appointed <dn>את</dn> duties to the priests and the Lěvites, each in his task, [31] and for <dn>את</dn> the wood offering and the first-fruits at appointed times. Remember me, O my <dn>Elohim</dn>, for good!

readings.title: The Oracle to Israel
readings.subtitle: The message of the word of YeHoVaH to Israel through Malachi.
readings.text: [Malachi 1:1] The message of <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to Yisra’ěl by Mal’aḵi.

readings.title: Jacob Loved, Esau Hated
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH declares His sovereign love for Israel.
readings.text: [Malachi 1:2] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have loved <dn>את</dn> you,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. “But you asked, ‘In what way have <dn>You</dn> loved us?’ <dq>“Was not Ěsav Ya‛aqoḇ’s brother?”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> love <dn>את</dn> Ya‛aqoḇ,</dq> [3] <dq>but <dn>I</dn> have hated <dn>את</dn> Ěsav, and have laid waste <dn>את</dn> his mountains and <dn>את</dn> his inheritance for the jackals of the wilderness.”</dq> [4] If Eḏom says, “We have been beaten down, let us return and build the ruins,” <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts said thus: <dq>“Let them build, but <dn>I</dn> tear down. And they shall be called ‘Border of Wrongness’, and <dn>את</dn> the people against whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is enraged forever.</dq> [5] <dq>And your eyes shall see, and you shall say, ‘Great is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> beyond the border of Yisra’ěl!’</dq>

readings.title: Polluted Offerings
readings.subtitle: The priests are accused of despising the Name of YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [Malachi 1:6] <dq>“A son esteems <dn>את</dn> his father, and a servant <dn>את</dn> his master. And if <dn>I</dn> am the Father, where is <dn>My</dn> esteem? And if <dn>I</dn> am a Master, where is <dn>My</dn> fear?</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts to you priests who despise <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Name. But you asked, ‘In what way have we despised <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> Name?’ [7] <dq>“You are presenting defiled food on <dn>My</dn> slaughter-place. But you asked, ‘In what way have we defiled <dn>את</dn> <dn>You</dn>?’ Because you say, ‘The table of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is despicable.’</dq> [8] <dq>“And when you present <dn>את</dn> the blind as a slaughtering, is it not evil? And when you present <dn>את</dn> the lame and sick, is it not evil? Bring it then to your governor! Would he be pleased with you? Would he accept <dn>את</dn> you favourably?”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts.

readings.title: A Prophecy to the Nations
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH declares His Name will be great among the nations.
readings.text: [Malachi 1:9] <dq>“And now, entreat <dn>את</dn> the face of Ěl to show favour to us. This has been done by your hands. Would <dn>He</dn> show favour to you?”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts. [10] <dq>“Who among you who would shut <dn>את</dn> the doors, so that you would not kindle fire on <dn>My</dn> slaughter-place for naught? <dn>I</dn> have no pleasure in you,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“Nor do <dn>I</dn> accept an offering from your hands.</dq> [11] <dq>“For from the rising of the sun, even to its going down, <dn>My</dn> Name is great among nations. And in every place incense is presented to <dn>My</dn> Name, and a clean offering. For <dn>My</dn> Name is great among nations,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts.

readings.title: Contempt for the Lord's Table
readings.subtitle: The priests' weariness and deceitful sacrifices are condemned.
readings.text: [Malachi 1:12] <dq>“But you are profaning <dn>את</dn> <dn>Me</dn>, in that you say, ‘The table of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is defiled, and its fruit, its food, is despicable.’</dq> [13] <dq>“And you said, ‘Oh, what weariness!’ and you sneered at it,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts. <dq>“And you brought in <dn>את</dn> plunder, and <dn>את</dn> the lame, and <dn>את</dn> the sick – thus you have brought in <dn>את</dn> the offering! Should <dn>I</dn> accept this from your hand?”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [14] <dq>“But cursed be the deceiver who has a male in his flock, and makes a vow, but is slaughtering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>את</dn> what is blemished. For <dn>I</dn> am a great Sovereign,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“and <dn>My</dn> Name is feared among nations.</dq>

readings.title: A Command and a Curse
readings.subtitle: A warning is issued to the priests who do not honor God's Name.
readings.text: [Malachi 2:1] <dq>“And now, O priests, this command is for you.</dq> [2] <dq>“If you do not hear, and if you do not take it to heart, to give esteem to <dn>My</dn> Name,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall send <dn>את</dn> a curse upon you, and <dn>I</dn> shall curse <dn>את</dn> your blessings. And indeed, <dn>I</dn> have cursed them, because you do not take it to heart.</dq> [3] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> shall rebuke your seed, and scatter <dn>את</dn> dung before your faces, <dn>את</dn> the dung of your festivals. And you shall be taken away with it.</dq> [4] <dq>“And you shall know that <dn>I</dn> have sent <dn>את</dn> this command to you, as being <dn>My</dn> covenant with <dn>את</dn> Lěvi,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts.

readings.title: The Corruption of the Priesthood
readings.subtitle: The ideal priest is contrasted with the corrupt priests of Malachi's day.
readings.text: [Malachi 2:5] <dq>“<dn>My</dn> covenant with him was life and peace, and <dn>I</dn> gave them to him, to fear. And he feared <dn>Me</dn>, and stood in awe of <dn>My</dn> Name.</dq> [6] <dq>“The Torah of truth was in his mouth, and unrighteousness was not found on his lips. <dn>He</dn> walked with <dn>Me</dn> in peace and straightness, and turned many away from crookedness.</dq> [7] <dq>“For the lips of a priest should guard knowledge, and they seek the Torah from his mouth, for he is the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts.</dq> [8] <dq>“But you, you have turned from the way, you have caused many to stumble in the Torah. You have corrupted <dn>את</dn> the covenant of Lěvi,”</dq> said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts. [9] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> also, <dn>I</dn> shall make <dn>את</dn> you despised and low before all the people, because you are not guarding <dn>My</dn> ways, and are showing partiality in the Torah.”</dq>
